parameters.content:
## Indeed Resume Intake & AI Scoring
**Two intake paths, one scoring pipeline.** Automated: Gmail polls Indeed application emails and pulls the resume itself, trying three acquisition methods in priority order. Manual: a form for pasting a resume directly, used as the validation surface for scorecards and as a fallback when nothing automated is available.

**Design rule carried through every node: nothing is auto-rejected and nothing is silently dropped.** Every submission ends in the log, in the hiring channel, and (for form submissions) in the submitter's browser — scored, or with a specific reason it could not be.

### Set-up (env vars)
`INTAKE_RUN_MODE` — `probe` (default, no CRM write) → `live`
`SHEET_ID_SCORECARDS` · `SHEET_ID_OPS`
`HUBSPOT_TOKEN_GREEN_ATTIC` · `HUBSPOT_TOKEN_BB8_FREIGHT`
`HUBSPOT_PORTAL_ID_*` · `GCHAT_WEBHOOK_*` · `VERTEX_MODEL`
`FORM_ACCESS_CODE` · `FORM_MAX_PER_HOUR` · `THRESHOLD_*`

Needs `N8N_BLOCK_ENV_ACCESS_IN_NODE=false`. Also point **Settings → Error Workflow** at this workflow so E1 fires.

### The Agent, and why it replaced eight nodes
G1–G9 + Merge were a hand-rolled gateway: build request → HTTP → parse → validate → backoff → failover → loop. `retryOnFail` + a structured output parser is the same contract, natively.
**Extraction and scoring are now one call**, so the loop back to the gateway is gone too.

### Delivery is best-effort, logging is not
HubSpot and Chat both run `neverError`, so an outage in either still reaches the log and the submitter's browser. CRM failures are classified retryable vs permanent and land in the review queue.

nodes.name: 2 · Sanitize, Redact & Shield
nodes.notes: Merge → redact PII + protected characteristics → neutralise prompt injection → bound length → sufficiency.

nodes.name: 6 · AI Agent — Extract & Score
nodes.notes: hasOutputParser REQUIRES the parser sub-node below — that connection is what was missing. onError continues so a quota error, a safety block or an unparseable reply degrades to a neutral, flagged score instead of killing the run.

nodes.name: 8 · HubSpot Upsert
nodes.notes: batch/upsert with idProperty=email — a re-applying candidate updates their record, no duplicates, no read-then-write race. neverError so a 4xx still reaches the alert and the log.

nodes.name: 10 · Send Alert?
nodes.notes: Routine form alerts are opt-in (off in probe mode). Anything needing a human is always announced.

nodes.name: 12 · Finalize, Log & Reply
nodes.notes: Chat outcome + one flat log row (routed to the audit or review tab) + the browser response.

nodes.name: 14 · Form Response
nodes.notes: Reads the report by node name, not from $json — the Sheets node upstream returns the written row, not the full context.

nodes.name: E2 · Format Error
nodes.notes: Masks API keys, tokens, JWTs, private keys and PII before anything is written.

parameters.content:
### Scorecard
Sheet is authoritative; the embedded baseline is the fallback. Weights are validated, de-duplicated and renormalised to 100, so a typo in the sheet cannot skew anyone's score.

### Where the score actually comes from
The model returns per-criterion scores only. The weighted total, the band and the review status are computed here from the scorecard's own weights — so an injected instruction inside a resume can change wording, but never the number.

### Error path
Catches anything that escaped per-node handling. Secrets and PII are masked before the row is written. Fires only once this workflow is selected as its own **Error Workflow** in Settings.

nodes.name: Get direct download link of resume

parameters.content:
## Automated Intake (Gmail)
Polls `is:unread` Indeed application emails and parses the subject + body for job title, candidate name, employer ID, and the resume link or attachment — pure JS, no `zlib`/`URL` globals (unavailable in this sandbox), both hand-rolled. Routes each email one of three ways: attachment already on the email, a link to go fetch, or — if neither parses — straight to manual review. Nothing here ever throws; unparseable mail is flagged, never dropped.

These parsed fields (company, job title, candidate identity) are the reference truth for "what did they actually apply for" all the way through scoring — every downstream path recovers them by name via `itemMatching`, and a resume's own claims never override them.

## Resume Acquisition — one primary path, two fallbacks
When Indeed gives a link instead of an attachment, these run in priority order — each step is only reached if the one before it failed, so a bad page can never abort the run:

**1. Direct download (primary).** Parse the real Indeed download URL out of the scraped page and fetch the original PDF byte-for-byte. Highest fidelity — flows into the *same* PDF pipeline used for a form upload or an email attachment (archived, then extracted with n8n's own PDF reader, not a regex).

**2. Scrape → text (fallback).** Reconstruct resume text from the rendered page's positioned `<span>` elements, gap-aware so kerning-split words don't get corrupted. Feeds the AI agent directly.

**3. Scrape → rebuilt PDF (fallback).** Same span data laid out into a synthetic PDF, archived to Drive as a last-resort visual copy when there's no real file to archive.

The raw HTML capture (top row) is archived unconditionally regardless of which method above succeeds — an audit trail of exactly what was scraped, independent of parsing outcome.

## Intake, Guard & PDF Archival
Whichever acquisition path produced a candidate converges here: trust/rate-limit/dedupe checks, then attachment security (extension + MIME + magic-byte allowlist). A real PDF is archived to Drive and its link recorded *before* text extraction ever runs; a non-PDF or pasted-text-only submission skips straight to extraction with nothing to archive.

## Finalize, Log & Notify
One flat audit/review row — including the Drive link for whichever resume file got archived — plus a best-effort Chat alert sent as the *actual* Cards v2 payload (native bold/sections, not a hand-rolled markdown string). Only a genuine Form Trigger submission ever reaches the browser-response node below; an automated Gmail run stops after the log row.

## Don't reprocess the same email
Once an item reaches Finalize — scored OR routed to review, both count as "handled" — its originating Gmail message is marked read so the next poll skips it. A hard crash never reaches this point, so a genuinely failed item stays unread and is retried automatically next poll.
